_disclaimer: General guidance only. Confirm with your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or agriculture officer before applying any chemical, and follow the product label.

Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Fungus (Venturia inaequalis) that overwinters in fallen leaves and spreads in cool, wet spring weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves and fruit; leaves may yellow and drop early.
prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn.
Prune to open the canopy so leaves dry quickly.
treatment: Remove badly infected leaves and fruit.
Use a recommended protectant fungicide during wet spring weather, as advised locally.

Apple___Black_rot.cause: Fungus (Botryosphaeria obtusa) living in dead wood, cankers and mummified fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-bordered 'frog-eye' leaf spots; fruit rots with concentric black rings.
prevention: Prune out dead branches and cankers.
Remove mummified fruit from tree and ground.
treatment: Cut infected limbs well below the canker and destroy them.
Apply a locally recommended fungicide from petal fall.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Fungus (Gymnosporangium) that alternates between apple and juniper/cedar trees.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface, later tube-like growths underneath.
prevention: Remove nearby juniper or cedar hosts if practical.
treatment: Remove infected leaves.
Protectant fungicide from pink bud stage, as locally advised.

prevention: Maintain balanced fertilisation and good drainage.
Prune for airflow and clear fallen debris.
treatment: No treatment needed.
No treatment needed.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.cause: Fungus (Podosphaera) favoured by warm days, cool nights and crowded canopies.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves; leaves may curl or distort.
prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen that causes soft growth.
Water at the base, not overhead.
treatment: Remove heavily infected shoots.
Use a sulphur-based or other locally recommended fungicide early in the outbreak.
No treatment needed.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.cause: Fungus (Cercospora zeae-maydis) that survives in crop residue, worse in humid weather.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular grey-tan lesions running parallel to leaf veins.
prevention: Bury or remove infected residue after harvest.
Use tolerant hybrids and avoid dense planting.
treatment: Apply a recommended foliar fungicide if disease reaches upper leaves before tasselling.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Fungus (Puccinia sorghi), spread by wind-borne spores in cool, humid conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, round, reddish-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces.
prevention: Plant early to avoid peak spore season.
treatment: Fungicide is rarely needed; consider it only for severe early infections, as locally advised.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Fungus (Exserohilum turcicum) surviving on residue, favoured by moderate temperatures and long leaf wetness.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions, 3-15 cm.
treatment: Apply a recommended foliar fungicide if lesions appear before or at tasselling.
No treatment needed.

Grape___Black_rot.cause: Fungus (Guignardia bidwellii) overwintering on mummified berries and canes.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots with dark borders; berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
prevention: Remove mummified berries and infected canes.
Train and prune for airflow and sunlight.
treatment: Apply a recommended fungicide from early shoot growth through fruit set.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: Complex of wood-rotting fungi entering through pruning wounds.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe yellow/brown patterns between leaf veins; dark spots on berries; vine decline.
prevention: Prune in dry weather and protect large cuts.
treatment: No reliable cure; remove and burn badly affected vines or trunks.
Consult an expert for trunk-renewal options.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.cause: Fungus (Pseudocercospora vitis) favoured by warm, humid weather.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on leaves, which may merge and cause early leaf fall.
treatment: Remove infected leaves.
Use a locally recommended fungicide if spreading.
No treatment needed.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Bacterium (Candidatus Liberibacter) spread by the Asian citrus psyllid insect.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy yellow mottling of leaves, small lopsided bitter fruit, twig dieback.
prevention: Scout often and report suspected trees.
treatment: No cure. Remove and destroy confirmed infected trees to protect others.
Contact your local horticulture or agriculture department immediately.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterium (Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni) spread by rain splash and wind.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small angular water-soaked spots turning purple-brown; 'shot-hole' leaves; spotted fruit.
prevention: Keep trees balanced, not over-fertilised with nitrogen.
treatment: Copper-based sprays as locally advised (timing is critical).
Remove severely affected twigs.
No treatment needed.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterium (Xanthomonas) carried on seed and debris, spread by splashing water.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves, yellow halos, raised scabby spots on fruit.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed or transplants.
Rotate away from peppers and tomatoes for 2-3 years.
Avoid working in wet fields; water at the base.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants.
Copper-based sprays may slow spread; follow local advice.
No treatment needed.

Potato___Early_blight.cause: Fungus (Alternaria solani) that survives in soil and debris; common on stressed, older plants.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings ('target' pattern) on older leaves, with yellowing.
prevention: Keep plants well fed and watered to reduce stress.
treatment: Remove heavily infected leaves.
Apply a recommended protectant fungicide at first symptoms.

Potato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete (Phytophthora infestans) that spreads very fast in cool, wet, humid weather.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large dark water-soaked blotches on leaves, white mould underneath in humid conditions, rotting tubers.
prevention: Destroy volunteer plants and cull piles.
Avoid overhead irrigation and late-evening watering.
Hill up soil to protect tubers.
treatment: Act immediately: this disease can destroy a field in days.
Apply a locally recommended fungicide on a protective schedule.
Destroy infected foliage; delay harvest until vines are dead.

prevention: Scout, especially in cool, wet weather.
treatment: No treatment needed.
No treatment needed.
No treatment needed.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.cause: Fungi (Podosphaera / Erysiphe) favoured by warm days, humid nights and dense foliage.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves; leaves yellow, dry and die early.
prevention: Water at the base, in the morning.
treatment: Remove badly affected leaves.
Use sulphur or another locally recommended fungicide early.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.cause: Fungus (Diplocarpon earlianum) spread by rain splash.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small purple spots that enlarge; leaf edges look scorched and dry.
treatment: Remove infected leaves.
Apply a locally recommended fungicide if severe.

prevention: Use mulch to keep fruit off soil.
treatment: No treatment needed.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacteria (Xanthomonas) on seed and debris, spread by splashing water and handling.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark greasy spots on leaves, often with yellow halos; rough scabby spots on fruit.
prevention: Use clean seed and healthy transplants.
Rotate away from tomato/pepper for 2-3 years.
Avoid overhead watering and don't handle wet plants.
treatment: Remove infected plants where severe.
Copper-based sprays can reduce spread; follow local advice.

Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Fungus (Alternaria solani) living in soil and debris, favoured by warm, humid weather.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on lower leaves, yellowing, leaf drop; dark sunken spots on stems and fruit.
prevention: Stake and prune lower leaves for airflow.
treatment: Remove affected lower leaves.
Apply a recommended protectant fungicide at first signs.

Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete (Phytophthora infestans) spreading rapidly in cool, wet, humid weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large greasy grey-green to brown blotches on leaves and stems, white mould underneath, firm brown fruit rot.
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation and leaf wetness.
Space plants well and stake them.
treatment: Act fast: remove and destroy infected plants (do not compost).
Apply a locally recommended fungicide to protect healthy plants nearby.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cause: Fungus (Passalora fulva), common in high humidity, especially in greenhouses and poly-houses.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surface with olive-green velvety mould underneath.
treatment: Remove infected leaves.
Use a locally recommended fungicide if spreading.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus (Septoria lycopersici) surviving on debris, spread by rain splash.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small circular spots with dark borders and grey centres on lower leaves.
treatment: Remove infected leaves early.
Apply a recommended protectant fungicide.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cause: Tiny two-spotted spider mites (not a disease) that thrive in hot, dry, dusty conditions.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow speckling on leaves, fine webbing underneath, bronzed dry leaves.
prevention: Keep plants well watered; avoid drought stress.
Protect natural predators; avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays.
treatment: Spray leaf undersides with strong water jets.
Use neem oil, insecticidal soap or a recommended miticide as locally advised.

Tomato___Target_Spot.cause: Fungus (Corynespora cassiicola), favoured by warm, humid weather and dense foliage.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings and yellow halos on leaves; sunken spots on fruit.
prevention: Improve airflow by staking and pruning.
treatment: Remove infected leaves.
Use a recommended fungicide if the disease spreads.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Virus spread by whiteflies; it does not spread through contact or water.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward-curled, crumpled yellow leaves, stunted plants, flower drop and poor fruit set.
prevention: Control whiteflies (yellow sticky traps, insect-proof nets in nurseries).
Use healthy seedlings and remove weeds that host whiteflies.
treatment: No cure: uproot and destroy infected plants early.
Manage whiteflies on the remaining crop as locally advised.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Virus spread by contaminated hands, tools, seed and plant debris; very stable and persistent.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic leaves, distorted or fern-like growth, uneven fruit ripening.
prevention: Use certified virus-free seed or resistant varieties.
Wash hands and disinfect tools between plants.
Avoid tobacco handling before touching plants.
Remove and destroy infected plants and debris.
treatment: No cure: remove and destroy infected plants (do not compost).

prevention: Scout weekly, especially in humid weather.
treatment: No treatment needed.
